From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Audit evidence request — admin activity scope, retention & export options

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise runbook and what we can provide out of the box. I'll attach a manifest template and redaction pattern examples in a follow-up.

High level (summary):
- Logged events: admin sign-ins, token/API key creation/deletion/rotation, role/grant changes, privilege elevation requests, console UI actions (create/delete/config changes), service-account actions, operator impersonation attempts, authentication failures, session termination. Each event includes timestamp (UTC), actor (email + internal id), target resource id, action type, request_id, and raw JSON payload where applicable.
- Retention: default 90 days in hot storage; archived exports available for 1–7 years based on contract. Extended retention is a reserved-capacity add-on (Dedicated/Private) and can be configured per-account.
- Export formats: compressed CSV, newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON), and compressed Parquet (for large volumes).
- Delivery methods: SFTP (preferred for automation), signed HTTPS download with time-limited URL, or direct HubDrive share with signed manifest. We also support streaming Syslog/CloudTrail-style delivery to customer collectors for real-time ingestion.
- Redaction & sampling: we can apply deterministic redaction rules (PII tokenization), field-level hashing (salted SHA256), or full field redaction. For sampling: we support time-window sampling, event-type sampling, and deterministic user-id bucketing to ensure reproducible samples. Sampling and redaction are applied at extract time and recorded in the manifest.
- Chain-of-custody: every export includes a manifest.csv that lists file names, event time range, record counts, and a SHA256 checksum per file. Manifests are signed with a Redwood HSM-backed key; we can also provide an attestation statement signed by our Compliance lead.

Limitations/notes:
- Deleted-object preimages: we keep action metadata (who deleted what and when) but full object preimages are stored only if the object was mutated within the last 30 days in the hot cache. Longer preimage retention requires custom retention policies.
- Timezones: all timestamps normalized to UTC in the export; we include original timezone offsets when available.
- PII sampling: sampled exports will not preserve cross-file referencability unless you request deterministic bucketing by user id.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will produce an export runbook (attached) with sample manifest and redaction map.
2) Kimberly will confirm the exact NDJSON/CSV schemas and provide a sample CSV slice.
3) Marissa will coordinate secure transfer scheduling and provide SFTP credentials or a HubDrive share link.

If that plan works I'll aim to have the sample artifacts to you by EOD Wed (Aug 4).

Thanks,
Ben 
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@medicosys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit evidence request — admin activity scope, retention & export options

Alice — attaching a sample slice and schema notes (see attachments stub). A few technical clarifications: 

- Fields included in NDJSON export (sample): event_ts_utc, actor_email, actor_id, resource_type, resource_id, action, result, ip_address, user_agent, request_id, trace_id, payload_snippet (truncated JSON up to 1024 chars).
- Redaction options: 
  * tokenization (pseudonymous_id): stable mapping per-tenant with rotation window (default 90 days)
  * deterministic hashing (salted per-export) — we record the salt in the manifest but don't share it by default; we can create a hashed-id mapping file under NDA.
  * regex-based redaction map (we run a dry-run to show before/after counts).
- Sampling mechanics: we support both deterministic bucketing by actor_id and uniform random sampling by event type. Deterministic bucketing ensures same user falls into sample across exports.
- Export packaging: exports >2GB are split into chunked parquet files and referenced from the manifest. We compute per-file SHA256 and a top-level bundle SHA256.

Attachments (referenced):
- admin-activity-manifest.csv (template)
- pii-redaction-map.pdf (examples and regex list)
- sample-admin-ndjson.gz (1000 events) — note: sample contains synthetic data and redaction examples.

Let us know which redaction approach you prefer for the Sig packet. If you want the salt mapping we will need a narrow NDA and an agreed key custody approach.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
